**Independent solution.** Put $\omega$ at the origin with $\ell: y=-5$, so $P,Q=(\pm12,-5)$. For $Y=(13c,13s)$, the tangency points on $\ell$ are:

- internal circle above $\ell$ (needs $s>-5/13$): $x=\dfrac{8c}{1+s}$
- internal circle below $\ell$ (needs $s<-5/13$): $x=\dfrac{18c}{1-s}$
- external circle above $\ell$ (needs $s>-5/13$): $x=\dfrac{18c}{1-s}$
- external circle below $\ell$ (needs $s<-5/13$): $x=\dfrac{8c}{1+s}$

Since $\omega_1,\omega_2$ share the tangency point $D$, they must lie on opposite sides of $\ell$. Checking both mixed cases, one of them gives $\omega_1$ below $\ell$ and $\omega_2$ above $\ell$. Using $\overline{YD}=\overline{YE}$, which means $x_D+x_E=26c_Y$, the constraints reduce to $s_Y=0$ and $s_X=-65/97$, with $c_Y=\pm1$.

Take $Y=(13,0)$. Then:

- $D=(8,-5)$ (radius of $\omega_2$ is 5)
- $E=(18,-5)$ (external circle at $X$ meets $\ell$ here)
- $F=(18,-5)$ (radius of $\omega_4$ is 5, center $(18,0)$)

Check: $\overline{YD}=\overline{YE}=5\sqrt2$, so the constraint holds. Therefore $\overline{YF}=5\sqrt2$.

The other mixed case gives the mirror-image configuration with the same $\overline{YF}$. The case with $\omega_1$ above $\ell$ and $\omega_2$ below forces $s_X > -5/13$ and $s_Y < -5/13$, which contradicts the solution it produces, so it yields nothing.

So the correct answer is $5\sqrt2$, which none of the three proposed solutions gives.
